intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do eco-adventure combining adrenaline with stunning biodiversity.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through jungle canals in a guided boat tour spotting caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, sloths, and hundreds of tropical bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse parks with a certified naturalist guide who uses a spotting scope to reveal camouflaged sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, poison dart frogs, and scarlet macaws hidden in the lush rainforest canopy.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Evening
experiences.description: Walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest around the iconic Arenal Volcano, spotting toucans and poison dart frogs, then unwind at sunset in natural volcanic hot spring pools surrounded by jungle — a perfect blend of adventure and relaxation.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Trekking Expedition
experiences.description: Trek deep into one of the most biologically intense places on Earth, home to jaguars, tapirs, scarlet macaws, and four species of monkeys. A guided day hike through old-growth rainforest along the Sirena ranger station trail offers unmatched wildlife encounters in a pristine wilderness.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange a small amount of currency at the airport (use ATMs for better rates). Take a budget shuttle or shared bus to Aegean Bliss Resort on the beachfront. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the beach to get oriented with the surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest beachfront town on foot. Visit the local sodas (small family-run restaurants) near the resort for an authentic first dinner. Stroll along the beach at sunset and enjoy the warm coastal air.

meals.breakfast: Eat before or during the flight
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport — look for a local soda or bakery inside the terminal for a cheap casado or sandwich (~$5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a nearby local soda — try a classic Casado (rice, beans, plantains, salad, and protein) for ~$6–10

day_by_day.notes: Download the Moovit or Rome2Rio app for budget transport options. Bring small USD bills for tips and small purchases. February is dry season — expect sunny, warm weather perfect for beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront. Look for wildlife including howler monkeys in nearby trees, shore birds, and possibly sea turtles (February is nesting season in some areas). Bring binoculars if you have them. This is free and one of Costa Rica's best budget wildlife experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby national park or wildlife refuge accessible by local bus or shared shuttle. Explore jungle trails, spot iguanas, sloths, and tropical birds. Many parks charge a modest entry fee (~$10–18 for foreigners). Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area. Enjoy a casual dinner at a local restaurant. Watch for bioluminescent plankton in the ocean after dark if conditions allow — a magical free experience.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans with eggs) at a local soda near the resort — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from a local market (fruit, bread, cheese) to eat at the park — ~$3–5
meals.dinner: Grilled fish or chicken at a beachfront soda — ~$7–10

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a reusable water bottle to save money and reduce plastic waste. Many parks require advance online booking — check the SINAC (Costa Rica national parks) website. Wear closed-toe shoes for jungle trails.

day_by_day.morning: Book a budget zip-lining tour in the local area. Many operators near coastal regions offer canopy zip-line packages starting at ~$35–55 per person. Look for combo deals that include rappelling or Tarzan swings. Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After zip-lining, cool off with a swim at the beach near the resort. Explore tide pools along the rocky sections of the coast for crabs, starfish, and small marine life — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town for a budget dinner. Try a local pulpería (convenience store/small market) for snacks and drinks, then find a soda for a full meal. Look for happy hour deals at beachside bars for a budget-friendly drink.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and toast at a local café — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Light meal at the zip-line operator's onsite café or bring your own snacks — ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Arroz con pollo or fresh ceviche at a local soda — ~$6–9

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining in advance during high season (February is peak). Compare at least 2–3 operators for price. Secure loose items before zip-lining. Wear comfortable athletic clothing and closed-toe shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning wildlife hike in a nearby biological reserve or secondary forest. Hire a local guide for a 2–3 hour guided nature walk (~$15–25 per person) to spot monkeys, sloths, toucans, and poison dart frogs. Local guides provide incredible value and support the community.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local farmers market or artisan market in the nearest town. Browse fresh tropical fruits, local crafts, and souvenirs. Try exotic fruits like maracuyá (passion fruit), guanábana, and mamón chino. Budget ~$5–10 for tastings and small purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal if your accommodation has kitchen facilities, using ingredients from the market. Alternatively, enjoy dinner at a local soda. Spend the evening stargazing on the beach — Costa Rica's low light pollution makes for stunning skies.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto with natilla (sour cream) and fresh juice at the resort or local soda — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit and snacks from the farmers market — ~$3–5
meals.dinner: Simple home-cooked pasta or rice dish using market ingredients OR soda meal — ~$3–8

day_by_day.notes: Ask your hotel staff to recommend trusted local guides — they often have connections with affordable, knowledgeable naturalists. February mornings are ideal for wildlife spotting before the heat of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget shared shuttle or local bus to a nearby mangrove estuary or river ecosystem. Join an affordable kayak or boat tour (~$20–35) through the mangroves to spot crocodiles, caimans, herons, kingfishers, and roseate spoonbills.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the mangrove tour, visit a nearby waterfall accessible by a short hike. Many waterfalls near Costa Rica's coasts are free or charge a small landowner fee (~$2–5). Swim in the natural pool at the base for a refreshing afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Enjoy a relaxing evening on the beach. Find a local soda with an ocean view for dinner and watch the sunset while dining.

meals.breakfast: Scrambled eggs, gallo pinto, and fresh fruit at a local soda — ~$4–6
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the waterfall — buy supplies at a local mini-super (small grocery) — ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Whole fried fish (pescado entero) with rice and salad at a beachfront soda — ~$8–12

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes for waterfall hikes — trails can be slippery. Apply reef-safe sunscreen before swimming. Bring a dry bag for electronics during the kayak/boat tour. Crocodile tours are safe when conducted by experienced local guides.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to snorkeling at a nearby reef or rocky point. Rent basic snorkel gear from a local shop (~$10–15/day) or join a budget group snorkel tour (~$25–40). Look for sea turtles, rays, tropical fish, and moray eels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue center or animal sanctuary in the region. Many centers charge a modest entry fee (~$15–25) and offer guided tours where you can see rescued sloths, monkeys, birds, and reptiles up close. These centers are budget-friendly and deeply educational.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local town's nightlife on a budget. Look for free live music at beachside bars or restaurants. Enjoy a local Imperial or Pilsen beer (~$2–3) and socialize with other travelers.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes and coffee at a local café — ~$4–6
meals.lunch: Casado at a soda near the wildlife center — ~$6–9
meals.dinner: Street food or food truck near the beach — try chifrijo (beans, rice, pork, chips) or empanadas — ~$4–7

day_by_day.notes: Check that the wildlife rescue center is a legitimate conservation organization (not a tourist trap). Avoid centers that allow handling of wild animals for photos. February's clear water makes snorkeling visibility excellent.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and lounge on the resort's beachfront. Take a morning yoga session on the beach (some resorts offer free or low-cost classes) or simply meditate to the sound of the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle from a local shop (~$8–15/day) and cycle along the coastal road or through nearby villages. This is an excellent budget way to explore the surrounding area, discover hidden beaches, and interact with locals.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to mark the halfway point of your trip. Look for a mid-range restaurant offering fresh seafood — budget ~$12–18 for a special meal. Enjoy a tropical cocktail like a guaro sour or piña colada.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — fresh fruit plate, yogurt, and coffee — ~$4–7
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda during your bike ride — try tamales or a quick bocas (appetizers) — ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant — grilled mahi-mahi or shrimp ceviche — ~$12–18

day_by_day.notes: This is a rest day — pace yourself. Costa Rica's heat can be exhausting, especially during peak dry season. Stay hydrated and wear a hat while cycling. Lock your bicycle when stopping.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby national park or protected area not yet visited. Research options within 1–2 hours of the resort. Pack a full day bag with water, snacks, sunscreen, and insect repellent. Enter the park early to maximize wildlife sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Look for scarlet macaws, toucans, monkeys, coatis, and if lucky, a tapir or jaguar track. Follow marked trails and respect all wildlife — maintain a safe distance at all times.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by late afternoon. Grab dinner at a local soda and share stories with fellow travelers at the hotel. Review your wildlife photos and journal about the day's sightings.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — gallo pinto and eggs to go from a local soda — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a scenic viewpoint in the park — fruit, sandwiches, trail mix — ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Comforting casado at a neighborhood soda — ~$6–9

day_by_day.notes: Check park opening hours and entry fees in advance on the SINAC website. Some parks require reservations. Bring a field guide app like iNaturalist to identify plants and animals. Wear neutral-colored clothing — bright colors can disturb wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Join a budget surfing lesson on the beach (~$25–40 for a 2-hour group lesson including board rental). Costa Rica's Pacific coast has excellent beginner-friendly waves in February. Even if you don't plan to surf regularly, it's a fun and memorable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After surfing, visit a local chocolate farm or coffee plantation tour if available in the area (~$15–25). Learn about cacao cultivation, fermentation, and chocolate making — and sample fresh chocolate. Many tours include tastings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the beach for a bonfire gathering if permitted, or join other travelers at a budget hostel's common area for a social evening. Play cards, share travel tips, and enjoy the relaxed Pura Vida atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before surfing — banana, granola bar, and coffee — ~$2–4
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut and fruit from a beach vendor, plus a soda meal — ~$5–7
meals.dinner: Pizza or pasta at a budget Italian-tico fusion restaurant (common in tourist areas) — ~$7–11

day_by_day.notes: Surfing lessons are widely available on most Costa Rican beaches. Book with a certified instructor. Apply waterproof sunscreen before surfing — the water reflects UV rays intensely. Chocolate farm tours are excellent for eco-tourism and supporting local farmers.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided bird-watching walk at dawn (~$15–25 with a local guide). Costa Rica has over 900 bird species — February is an excellent time for spotting migrants and resident species. Look for resplendent quetzals (if in highland areas), scarlet macaws, trogons, and hummingbirds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local indigenous community or cultural center if available in the region. Many communities offer guided tours that explain traditional practices, medicinal plants, and crafts (~$10–20). This supports local economies directly.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at the beach. Watch for green sea turtles coming ashore if near a nesting beach (February can be active). Join a guided turtle watching tour (~$20–30) — always use certified operators who follow conservation guidelines.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn snack before bird-watching — granola bar and water, then a proper breakfast after — gallo pinto at a soda — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Traditional meal at the indigenous community or nearby soda — ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Light dinner — fresh fruit, cheese, and crackers from a local mini-super — ~$4–6

day_by_day.notes: Bird-watching is best in the first 2 hours after sunrise. Speak quietly and move slowly on trails. Turtle watching tours must be done with licensed guides to protect nesting females. Never use flash photography near turtles.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a nearby waterfall hike you haven't visited yet, or revisit a favorite spot. Many areas near Costa Rica's coasts have multiple accessible waterfalls within a short distance. Bring swimming gear for a refreshing dip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach that is less touristy — ask resort staff for recommendations on hidden or quieter beaches nearby. Spend the afternoon swimming, reading, and relaxing. Collect interesting shells or driftwood as free souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare for the end of the trip by organizing souvenirs and reviewing your budget. Enjoy a final big dinner at a local restaurant — try a traditional Olla de Carne (Costa Rican beef stew) or whole roasted chicken.

meals.breakfast: Pinto with eggs and fresh orange juice at a local café — ~$4–6
meals.lunch: Picnic at the hidden beach — sandwiches and tropical fruit from the mini-super — ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Traditional Costa Rican dinner at a well-reviewed local soda — Olla de Carne or roasted chicken — ~$8–12

day_by_day.notes: Ask locals (not just hotel staff) for hidden beach recommendations — they know the best spots. Be mindful of strong currents at isolated beaches. Always swim near others when possible.

day_by_day.morning: Final wildlife adventure — take a dawn boat tour on a nearby river or estuary to spot crocodiles, river otters, and waterbirds one last time (~$20–35 for a shared group tour). Bring your best camera settings and binoculars for final wildlife photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon doing last-minute souvenir shopping at local markets. Look for handmade items like wood carvings, woven baskets, and locally produced coffee or chocolate — items that directly support artisans. Budget ~$20–40 for gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory final dinner with fellow travelers or solo reflection. Splurge slightly on a nicer meal (~$15–20) to celebrate a successful eco-adventure trip. Toast with a local guaro cocktail or fresh coconut water.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat tour — quick gallo pinto and coffee to go — ~$3–4
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local market food stall — try a Caribbean-style rice and beans with coconut milk if available — ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a recommended local restaurant — seafood platter or mixed grill — ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: Purchase vacuum-sealed Costa Rican coffee at a local supermarket (not airport) for the best prices — it makes an excellent and affordable souvenir. Confirm departure logistics and transportation to the airport for the next day.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — soak in the last moments of the Costa Rican coastline. Take final photos, breathe in the ocean air, and reflect on 13 days of eco-adventure. Check out of the resort and settle any outstanding bills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Juan Santamaría International Airport via shared shuttle or public bus (book in advance — ~$10–20 for shared shuttle). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for travel time and check-in. Explore the airport's duty-free for last-minute coffee or chocolate purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Board your return flight. Carry memories of zip-lining through jungle canopies, spotting sloths and toucans, and living the Pura Vida lifestyle on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda — ~$3–5
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport — budget soda or sandwich shop — ~$6–10
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your shuttle booking the night before. Keep $29 USD (or equivalent colones) available for the Costa Rica airport departure tax if not already included in your ticket. Arrive at the airport at least 3 hours before international departures. Keep all receipts for budget tracking — a great 13-day eco-adventure is possible for $800–1,200 USD total including accommodation, food, activities, and transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do eco-adventure combining adrenaline with stunning biodiversity.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse parks with a certified naturalist guide who uses a spotting scope to reveal camouflaged sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, poison dart frogs, and scarlet macaws hidden in the lush rainforest canopy.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands at 1:00 PM.
day_by_day.afternoon: After clearing customs and collecting luggage (~1.5 hours), arrange private shuttle or shared transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront (~2–3 hours depending on location). Arrive, check in, and settle into your room. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront to get oriented and enjoy the ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at the beach bar while watching the sunset. Light exploration of the resort grounds and nearby beachfront area.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick bite at Juan Santamaría International Airport — try the airport café for a casado or empanadas.
meals.lunch: Snack at the airport or during the transfer stop — roadside soda (local diner) for a traditional gallo pinto plate (~$6–10).
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant — enjoy fresh ceviche, grilled fish of the day, and a local Imperial beer. Budget ~$20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Do not over-plan Day 1. Travel fatigue is real. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport for small purchases. Confirm any pre-booked tours for upcoming days at the resort concierge desk.

day_by_day.morning: After a good night's rest, enjoy a full Costa Rican breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning on the beach — swim, snorkel in the warm Pacific waters, or simply walk along the shoreline and look for wildlife such as pelicans, frigate birds, and hermit crabs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or take a guided stand-up paddleboard (SUP) tour along the coastline (~$25–40). Explore nearby sea caves or mangrove estuaries if available. Alternatively, visit a nearby local village for a cultural walk and fresh fruit shopping at a roadside market.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the beach (many resorts offer this complimentary or for ~$10–15). Freshen up and head out for dinner at a local beachfront restaurant in the nearby town.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet or à la carte at the resort — gallo pinto, eggs, tropical fruits, and fresh juice. Budget ~$12–18.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local soda near the beach — try arroz con pollo or a fresh fish taco plate. Budget ~$7–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range local seafood restaurant — whole grilled snapper, patacones (fried plantains), and a fresh coconut drink. Budget ~$18–25.

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — Costa Rica is very eco-conscious and many beaches require it. Bring a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided wildlife walk along a nearby nature trail or beach estuary. Look for howler monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, and iguanas with a local naturalist guide (~$30–45 per person for 2–3 hours). Best wildlife activity is always at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue and rehabilitation center nearby (e.g., a sloth sanctuary or butterfly garden). Learn about Costa Rica's conservation efforts and interact ethically with rescued animals. Entry ~$15–25.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a swim and rest. Try a cooking class at the resort or a nearby culinary studio — learn to make traditional Costa Rican dishes like olla de carne or tres leches cake (~$40–60).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the wildlife walk — grab fresh fruit, a granola bar, and coffee from the resort's grab-and-go station.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the wildlife center's café or a nearby soda — casado with beef or chicken, rice, beans, salad, and a natural fruit juice. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.dinner: Enjoy the meal you prepared in the cooking class, or dine at a local mid-range restaurant with traditional Costa Rican cuisine. Budget ~$15–22.

day_by_day.notes: Bring binoculars for the wildlife walk — they make a huge difference. Wear neutral-colored clothing (no bright colors) to avoid disturbing animals. Insect repellent is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the drive/transfer toward Manuel Antonio National Park (if not already nearby). Check in or store luggage at a mid-range lodge near the park entrance. Begin the **Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike** — a 3–4 hour certified naturalist-guided tour through one of the world's most biodiverse parks. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, two and three-toed sloths, poison dart frogs, and coatis.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, relax on Playa Manuel Antonio — one of Costa Rica's most beautiful beaches inside the national park. Swim, snorkel, or simply observe the wildlife that wanders onto the beach. The park closes at 4:00 PM so plan to exit by 3:30 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the town of Quepos (10–15 minutes from the park) for dinner and evening exploration. Walk along the marina, browse local craft shops, and enjoy the lively small-town atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or a café en route — gallo pinto and coffee is the classic Costa Rican start. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch or buy snacks from a vendor near the park entrance — fresh coconut water, fruit, and sandwiches. Budget ~$5–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Quepos at a mid-range restaurant overlooking the marina — try the fresh tuna ceviche and grilled lobster tail. Budget ~$22–35.

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park limits daily visitors — book tickets online in advance at sinac.go.cr. The park is closed on Mondays. Bring waterproof sandals as some trails have stream crossings. Do NOT feed the monkeys.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on the Río Savegre or Río Naranjo near Quepos — a thrilling Class III–IV rapids experience through lush jungle canyons. Full guided excursion with safety equipment, professional guides, and lunch included (~$65–90 per person). Suitable for beginners with a sense of adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from rafting and freshen up. Visit a local waterfall or natural swimming hole in the afternoon for a refreshing swim surrounded by rainforest. Many tour operators offer combo packages.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the beachfront area. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a sunset walk and light shopping for local crafts and souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before rafting — eggs, toast, tropical fruit, and strong Costa Rican coffee. Budget ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Lunch is typically included with the rafting tour — traditional casado served riverside. Included in tour cost.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a beachside open-air restaurant — grilled chicken, rice and beans, and a cold beer. Budget ~$14–20.

day_by_day.notes: Wear clothes you don't mind getting soaked. Secure all valuables in waterproof dry bags provided by the tour operator. Rafting is best during February as water levels are moderate and manageable.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the journey to Monteverde — approximately 4–5 hours by road (scenic mountain drive). Arrange a private shuttle or shared tourist shuttle (~$35–55 per person). The drive through the central highlands is stunning with views of volcanoes and coffee plantations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde, check into a mid-range eco-lodge or boutique hotel. Spend the afternoon visiting the Monteverde Butterfly Garden or Orchid Garden — a peaceful and educational introduction to the region's incredible biodiversity. Entry ~$12–18.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the main street of Santa Elena village — browse local artisan shops, try homemade cheese (Monteverde is famous for its dairy), and enjoy the cool mountain air (~1,400 meters elevation).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departure — pack a snack for the road. Budget ~$10–14.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda en route — try a traditional casado or empanadas. Budget ~$7–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Santa Elena at a cozy mid-range restaurant — try the Monteverde cheese fondue, homemade pasta, or local trout. Budget ~$16–24.

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde is partially unpaved and bumpy — a 4WD vehicle or shuttle is strongly recommended. Bring a light jacket as Monteverde is significantly cooler than the coast. Pack a rain poncho as afternoon mist and light rain is common.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of the trip — **Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour**! Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most iconic zip-line circuits. Multiple platforms, Tarzan swings, and a hanging bridge crossing await. Duration ~3 hours. Cost ~$45–75 per person. Book the earliest slot for the best misty cloud forest atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, visit the **Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve** — a 2–3 hour self-guided or guided walk through one of the most pristine cloud forests on Earth. Look for resplendent quetzals, emerald toucanets, and glass frogs. Entry ~$25, guided tour ~$35–50 extra.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a guided night tour of the cloud forest (~$25–35) — discover nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, sleeping birds, tarantulas, and glowing fungi. This is a truly magical experience unique to Monteverde.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the eco-lodge before the zip-line — fuel up with eggs, gallo pinto, and fresh tropical juice. Budget ~$10–16.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the zip-line operator's café or a nearby soda — sandwiches, fresh fruit, and lemonade. Budget ~$8–13.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Santa Elena — try the local cheese plate, grilled beef tenderloin, and a glass of Chilean wine. Budget ~$20–30.

day_by_day.notes: Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing for zip-lining. Weight and age restrictions may apply — check with the operator in advance. The cloud forest reserve has limited daily visitors — book tickets online in advance. Camera with a good zoom lens is highly recommended for quetzal spotting.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning birdwatching walk in the cloud forest with a specialized birding guide (~$40–60 for 3 hours). February is an excellent month for spotting the resplendent quetzal, which is in mating season. This is a bucket-list wildlife experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the **Selvatura Adventure Park** or **Sky Adventures Monteverde** for hanging bridges — walk 8 suspension bridges through the forest canopy at different heights for breathtaking views and more wildlife spotting. Cost ~$30–45.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local coffee and chocolate tour at a nearby farm — learn about Costa Rica's famous coffee production and cacao cultivation. Taste freshly brewed coffee and artisanal chocolate. Duration ~2 hours. Cost ~$20–30.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the early birdwatching — granola, yogurt, and coffee. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a farm-to-table café near the hanging bridges — fresh salads, homemade soups, and local cheeses. Budget ~$10–16.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant with live traditional marimba music — enjoy the cultural experience with a casado and fresh fruit smoothie. Budget ~$14–20.

day_by_day.notes: The resplendent quetzal is most active at dawn — set your alarm early. Bring a telephoto lens or ask your guide if they have a spotting scope. The coffee and chocolate tour is family-friendly and highly educational.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Monteverde and travel to Arenal Volcano area (~3–4 hours by shuttle via Lake Arenal ferry or road). The scenic Lake Arenal crossing by boat is a beautiful and efficient route (~$25–35 per person by shuttle). Check into a mid-range lodge with volcano views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the **Arenal Volcano National Park** for a guided hike on the lava fields trail — walk through the 1968 lava flow with views of the perfect cone-shaped Arenal Volcano. Guided tour ~$35–50. The volcano is active and the surrounding biodiversity is exceptional.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the famous **Tabacón Hot Springs** or **Ecotermales Hot Springs** — natural volcanic thermal pools surrounded by tropical gardens. Perfect for relaxing after days of adventure. Cost ~$40–75 (includes dinner buffet at some resorts).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure. Budget ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a lakeside soda near Lake Arenal — fresh fish from the lake, rice, and plantains. Budget ~$8–13.
meals.dinner: Dinner buffet included at the hot springs resort, or dine at a mid-range restaurant in La Fortuna town with views of the volcano. Budget ~$18–28.

day_by_day.notes: Arenal Volcano is often cloud-covered in the afternoon — mornings typically offer the clearest views. Book hot springs in advance as they fill up quickly. La Fortuna is the main town near Arenal and has excellent restaurants, ATMs, and tour operators.

day_by_day.morning: Guided **La Fortuna Waterfall** hike — descend 500+ steps through lush rainforest to reach the stunning 75-meter waterfall. Swim in the natural pool at the base. Entry ~$18, guided tour ~$30–45. Start early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: White-water kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal — enjoy panoramic views of the volcano from the water. Guided kayak tour ~$45–65. Alternatively, visit the **Arenal Hanging Bridges** for a 3km loop through primary rainforest with excellent wildlife spotting.
day_by_day.evening: Explore La Fortuna town — visit the local market, browse artisan shops, and enjoy the vibrant small-town atmosphere. Try local street food from market vendors.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast at the lodge before the waterfall hike — eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and coffee. Budget ~$10–16.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near the waterfall or at a nearby soda — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruit, and coconut water. Budget ~$7–11.
meals.dinner: Dinner in La Fortuna at a popular mid-range restaurant — try the volcano burger, local trout, or traditional casado with a cold local craft beer. Budget ~$16–24.

day_by_day.notes: The waterfall steps are steep and can be slippery — wear waterproof hiking shoes with grip. Bring a dry bag for your camera and valuables. The swimming area at the waterfall base is cold but incredibly refreshing.

day_by_day.morning: **Wildlife safari float** on the Peñas Blancas River — a gentle, non-whitewater float through pristine rainforest on inflatable tubes or a small raft with a naturalist guide. Spot caimans, river otters, Jesus Christ lizards, kingfishers, and monkeys. Duration ~3 hours. Cost ~$45–65.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the **Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge** (full-day option) or alternatively explore a local cacao farm for a hands-on chocolate-making workshop. The cacao tour is a wonderful cultural and culinary experience (~$30–45) and pairs beautifully with Costa Rica's eco-tourism mission.
day_by_day.evening: Return to La Fortuna for a final evening at the hot springs. Try **Baldi Hot Springs** for a more social atmosphere with multiple pools and a swim-up bar. Cost ~$35–55.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the lodge — yogurt, granola, fresh fruit, and coffee. Budget ~$8–12.
meals.lunch: Lunch included with the safari float tour, or eat at a local soda near the river. Budget ~$7–12.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in La Fortuna at a rooftop restaurant with volcano views — enjoy a three-course meal with local ingredients, a glass of wine, and a dessert of tres leches cake. Budget ~$22–32.

day_by_day.notes: The wildlife safari float is ideal for all ages and fitness levels — no experience required. Bring polarized sunglasses to reduce water glare and spot wildlife more easily. February is dry season in this region, making it ideal for outdoor activities.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal and travel back toward the Pacific coast / Aegean Bliss Resort (~4–5 hours by shuttle). Enjoy the scenic drive through the central highlands, coffee country, and down to the coast. Alternatively, stop at a coffee plantation near Naranjo or Palmares for a guided tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and spend the afternoon at leisure — relax on the beach, swim in the ocean, or book a spa treatment at the resort (~$50–90 for a 60-minute massage). You've earned it!
day_by_day.evening: Sunset catamaran cruise along the coastline — enjoy snorkeling, dolphin watching, and a spectacular Pacific sunset with drinks and snacks on board. Duration ~3–4 hours. Cost ~$65–90 per person.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure. Budget ~$10–15.
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda en route or at the coffee plantation café — fresh coffee, pastries, and a light meal. Budget ~$8–13.
meals.dinner: Dinner on the catamaran (light appetizers included) or at the resort's beachfront restaurant upon return — fresh grilled seafood platter and a tropical cocktail. Budget ~$20–30.

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran cruise in advance as spaces fill up quickly, especially during peak season (February). The sunset catamaran is one of the most memorable experiences in Costa Rica — highly recommended. Bring a light jacket for the boat ride as it can get breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica — wake up early for one last sunrise beach walk. Look for nesting sea turtles (depending on location and season) or simply collect shells and reflect on the incredible journey. Optional: final snorkeling session or paddleboard rental at the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort (typically 11:00 AM or 12:00 PM). Arrange a transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport. Allow at least 3–4 hours before your departure flight for travel time and airport check-in. Browse the airport's duty-free shops for last-minute souvenirs — coffee, chocolate, and local crafts are excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with unforgettable memories of cloud forests, volcanoes, wildlife, zip-lines, and pristine beaches. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final Costa Rican breakfast at the resort — savor every bite of gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, and locally grown coffee. Budget ~$12–18.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the airport or at the resort before checkout — ceviche, empanadas, and fresh juice. Budget ~$8–14.
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or grab a final Imperial beer and bocas (appetizers) at the airport bar before boarding. Budget ~$12–20.

day_by_day.notes: Pack all souvenirs in checked luggage — coffee and chocolate are fine in carry-on but declare any fresh food at customs. Do NOT attempt to bring any plants, seeds, or wildlife products — Costa Rica has strict agricultural inspection at the airport. Tip your guides, drivers, and hotel staff generously — 10–15% is standard and greatly appreciated.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring 15 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do eco-adventure combining adrenaline with stunning biodiversity.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through jungle canals in a guided boat tour spotting caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, sloths, and hundreds of tropical bird species. If visiting between July and October, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the beach at night.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse parks with a certified naturalist guide who uses a spotting scope to reveal camouflaged sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, poison dart frogs, and scarlet macaws hidden in the lush rainforest canopy.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Evening
experiences.description: Walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest around the iconic Arenal Volcano, spotting toucans and poison dart frogs, then unwind at sunset in natural volcanic hot spring pools surrounded by jungle — a perfect blend of adventure and relaxation.

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Jungle Trekking Expedition
experiences.description: Trek deep into one of the most biologically intense places on Earth, home to jaguars, tapirs, scarlet macaws, and four species of monkeys. A guided day hike through old-growth rainforest along the Sirena ranger station trail offers unmatched wildlife encounters in a pristine wilderness.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Private luxury transfer from Juan Santamaría International Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort awaits upon landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport meet-and-greet with a dedicated concierge. Scenic luxury transfer to the resort (approx. 2–3 hours depending on location). Check in, champagne welcome, and resort orientation tour. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind on your private terrace overlooking the Pacific.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar. Leisurely first dinner at the resort's signature restaurant to recover from travel and acclimate to Costa Rica's tropical atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at airport lounge prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or ceviche bites at resort upon arrival
meals.dinner: Signature restaurant at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh Pacific seafood tasting menu with curated Costa Rican wine and craft cocktail pairings

day_by_day.notes: Request early room preparation through the concierge in advance. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the resort's activity desk this evening. Hydrate well and apply sunscreen — February is dry season with intense sun.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the private beachfront terrace or resort wellness pavilion, followed by a guided snorkeling or paddleboard experience along the resort's protected cove — ideal for first-morning ocean immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided nature walk through the resort's surrounding coastal forest with a resident naturalist. Spot howler monkeys, white-faced capuchins, scarlet macaws, and coastal iguanas. Return to resort for a poolside lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in the resort's luxury spa with a signature Costa Rican volcanic stone massage and jungle botanical body wrap. Dinner under the stars on the resort's private beach with torchlit ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Lavish tropical breakfast buffet at the resort — fresh açaí bowls, local fruits, eggs Benedict, freshly squeezed guanábana juice
meals.lunch: Poolside gourmet lunch — grilled mahi-mahi tacos, hearts of palm salad, chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dining experience at Aegean Bliss Resort — five-course Costa Rican fusion menu with sommelier-selected wines

day_by_day.notes: This day is intentionally relaxed to allow full acclimatization before more intensive adventures begin. Book spa treatments in advance as slots fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private luxury vehicle toward Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 30–45 minutes from the resort area). Begin the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike with a certified naturalist guide equipped with a high-powered spotting scope. Search for three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchins, poison dart frogs, and nesting shorebirds along pristine jungle trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the guided hike through the park's interior, emerging at the iconic Playa Manuel Antonio — a postcard-perfect crescent beach framed by jungle. Enjoy a private picnic lunch on the beach before a leisurely swim in the calm cove. Return to the resort by private transfer in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Refresh at the resort, then enjoy cocktails at the resort's rooftop bar watching the Pacific sunset. Dinner at a premium local restaurant in the Manuel Antonio village.

meals.breakfast: Early continental breakfast at the resort before departure — fresh pastries, tropical fruit, Colombian coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic on Playa Manuel Antonio — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, tropical fruit, sparkling water
meals.dinner: La Cantina or equivalent premium restaurant in Manuel Antonio — whole grilled snapper, yuca fries, and local craft beers or tropical cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Manuel Antonio National Park early (gates open at 7:00 AM) to maximize wildlife sightings before midday heat. Wear lightweight, neutral-colored clothing and closed-toe shoes. Apply biodegradable sunscreen and insect repellent. Park has a daily visitor cap — pre-book tickets.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs toward the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado National Park (approximately 3–4 hours or optional 30-minute charter flight for ultimate luxury). Begin the Corcovado National Park Jungle Trekking Expedition with an expert naturalist guide — one of the most biodiverse places on Earth. Trek through old-growth primary rainforest searching for jaguars, Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, and scarlet macaws.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue deep-jungle trekking along the Sirena Ranger Station trails. Wade through shallow river crossings and traverse root-laden forest floors. Spot giant anteaters, poison dart frogs, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds. Enjoy a packed gourmet lunch at a jungle clearing.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort (or charter flight back). Soak tired muscles in the resort's hydrotherapy pool. Light dinner at the resort's wellness restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hearty pre-trek breakfast at the resort — scrambled eggs, gallo pinto (Costa Rican rice and beans), fresh fruit, strong coffee
meals.lunch: Premium packed jungle lunch — grain bowls, energy bars, fresh tropical fruit, electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Resort wellness restaurant — nourishing post-trek dinner of grilled chicken, quinoa, roasted vegetables, and herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is one of the world's most remote and pristine national parks — this is a bucket-list experience. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots, long pants, and long-sleeved shirts. Carry plenty of water. Consider the charter flight option (approx. 30 min vs. 4-hour drive) for a premium, time-efficient experience. Permits must be arranged well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Well-deserved rest and recovery morning at the resort. Sleep in, then enjoy a leisurely breakfast followed by a private yoga or Pilates session with the resort's in-house instructor on the ocean-facing pavilion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sport fishing charter departing from the resort's marina or nearest dock. Fish for marlin, sailfish, dorado, and yellowfin tuna in the Pacific's deep blue waters with an experienced captain and first mate. Snorkeling stop at a secluded offshore reef on the return.
day_by_day.evening: Have your catch prepared by the resort's executive chef in a special 'catch-to-table' private dinner on your terrace or in the resort's private dining room. Pair with premium Costa Rican craft spirits and fine wines.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte breakfast at the resort — eggs your way, smoked salmon, avocado toast, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light bites and refreshments aboard the fishing charter — ceviche, tropical fruit, cold beverages
meals.dinner: Private 'catch-to-table' chef's dinner at the resort — your fresh catch prepared with Costa Rican spices, accompanied by coconut rice and plantains

day_by_day.notes: February is excellent for sport fishing off Costa Rica's Pacific coast. Confirm fishing charter availability and licensing with the resort concierge. If fishing is not of interest, substitute with a private catamaran sunset cruise with snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs toward the Tortuguero region on the Caribbean coast (this typically involves a flight or a combination of road and boat transfer — arrange a private charter flight from a nearby airstrip for the premium experience, approximately 45 minutes). Arrive at the jungle lodge base and begin the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari — glide through labyrinthine jungle canals spotting caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, and river otters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat safari deeper into Tortuguero's canal network with your expert naturalist guide. Explore secondary channels where wildlife density is highest — look for green iguanas sunbathing on branches, Jesus Christ lizards running across the water's surface, and dozens of tropical bird species including kingfishers and herons. Arrive at a premium eco-lodge for a mid-afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Optional guided night walk along Tortuguero's beach (February may coincide with early leatherback sea turtle nesting season — subject to official park permissions and ranger availability). Dinner at the eco-lodge's gourmet restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before transfer — tropical fruit, granola, yogurt, coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the Tortuguero eco-lodge or riverside restaurant — Caribbean-style rice and beans, fresh fish, plantains
meals.dinner: Tortuguero eco-lodge fine dining — Caribbean lobster, coconut curry, tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small plane — the private charter flight is strongly recommended for the premium experience. Pack light for this overnight or day trip. Leatherback turtles begin nesting in February — check with the park's turtle monitoring program for guided, responsible beach visits. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort the following morning or stay overnight at the eco-lodge.

day_by_day.morning: If overnighting in Tortuguero: Early morning second boat safari at dawn — the best time for wildlife activity. Spot sleeping caimans, fishing herons, and early-rising monkeys before the heat of the day. Charter flight return to the resort area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort by private charter. Arrival by early afternoon — spend the rest of the day at leisure by the pool or beach. Enjoy a resort spa treatment: choose from a Costa Rican coffee scrub, aloe vera wrap, or couples' massage.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic sunset cocktail cruise departing from the resort's dock — private catamaran with a butler, fresh ceviche, and champagne as the sun dips into the Pacific. Return for dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast in Tortuguero — tropical fruits, eggs, gallo pinto, freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at Aegean Bliss Resort upon return — sushi rolls, shrimp ceviche, fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Resort's premium oceanfront restaurant — surf and turf with Costa Rican tenderloin and grilled lobster tail

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle transition day between the Caribbean coast adventure and the next phase of the itinerary. Use this afternoon to repack for the upcoming Arenal and Monteverde segments if any luggage transfer is needed.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs early toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours from the central Pacific coast, or consider a domestic charter flight to La Fortuna for maximum comfort). Check in to a premium Arenal-area lodge or continue as a day excursion from the resort if logistics allow. Begin the Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs experience — walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest canopy with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the hanging bridges trail, spotting toucans, morpho butterflies, howler monkeys, and the dramatic Arenal Volcano cone rising through the forest. Arrive at a premium hot springs resort (La Paz or Baldi Termae luxury circuit) for a long, relaxing thermal soak in mineral-rich volcanic waters surrounded by lush jungle.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset soak in the highest-temperature thermal pools as steam rises into the cool evening air. Dinner at the hot springs resort's gourmet restaurant or a nearby premium restaurant in La Fortuna.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — full Costa Rican breakfast with gallo pinto, eggs, fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at the hanging bridges reserve's restaurant or packed picnic — Costa Rican casado, fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Premium restaurant in La Fortuna — grilled meats, traditional Costa Rican stews, local craft beer and rum cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Arenal Volcano is most visible in the early morning before clouds gather — the hanging bridges walk is perfectly timed for this. February's dry season offers excellent visibility of the volcano. Book the premium hot springs circuit in advance to secure private pools or VIP access.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on the glassy surface of Lake Arenal — the volcano's reflection in the water at dawn is a world-class sight. Spot kingfishers, ospreys, and migratory waterfowl along the lakeshore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer toward Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 2–3 hours from Arenal via the scenic lake road). Check in to a premium Monteverde lodge. Take an introductory guided walk through the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve — spot resplendent quetzals (February is nesting season — prime viewing!), three-wattled bellbirds, and emerald toucanets in the misty forest.
day_by_day.evening: Guided night walk through the cloud forest with a specialist naturalist — spot kinkajous, sleeping birds, glass frogs, and giant stick insects by torchlight. Dinner at the lodge's fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the Arenal lodge or hotel before departure — eggs, tropical fruits, freshly baked bread, Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in a local café en route to Monteverde — traditional casado or vegetable soup
meals.dinner: Monteverde lodge fine dining — cloud forest-inspired menu with local trout, heart of palm salad, and artisan chocolate desserts

day_by_day.notes: February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde — a legendary bird considered one of the world's most beautiful. Hire the lodge's specialist quetzal guide for maximum sighting chances. Evenings in Monteverde are cool (15–18°C) — pack a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of the Monteverde segment: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience the forest from above on multiple lines, including a Superman-style line and a Tarzan swing over the forest canopy. This is a world-class eco-adventure experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery — walk through enclosed gardens alive with hundreds of exotic butterfly species and dozens of hummingbird species feeding at close range. Visit a premium artisan chocolate workshop for a bean-to-bar chocolate-making experience using locally grown cacao.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the Monteverde Sky Walk viewpoint over the Gulf of Nicoya. Farewell dinner in Monteverde before preparing for the return journey south.

meals.breakfast: Early energizing breakfast at the lodge before the zip-line tour — protein-rich eggs, granola, fresh fruit, strong coffee
meals.lunch: Café in Monteverde village — gourmet sandwiches, fresh juices, artisan coffee
meals.dinner: Premium Monteverde restaurant (Celajes Restaurant or equivalent) — cloud forest tasting menu with local wines and artisan spirits

day_by_day.notes: The zip-line canopy tour requires moderate physical fitness. Weight limits apply — confirm with the operator in advance. The cloud forest zip-line experience is distinct from lowland canopy tours — the mist, altitude, and biodiversity make it uniquely spectacular. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Final guided quetzal-spotting walk in Monteverde's primary cloud forest at dawn — the absolute best time for bird activity. Spend 2 hours with a specialist ornithologist guide before the forest fills with day visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer back toward the Pacific coast and Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 4–5 hours, or arrange a domestic charter flight for a 45-minute scenic flight over the volcanoes and coastline). Arrive at the resort and settle back into your beachfront suite.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — sunset cocktails on the beach, followed by a private chef's dinner on your terrace with a curated Costa Rican menu prepared exclusively for you.

meals.breakfast: Final Monteverde lodge breakfast — eggs, gallo pinto, local cheeses, tropical fruit, cloud forest honey
meals.lunch: Gourmet en-route lunch stop or in-flight snacks if taking charter — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Private terrace chef's dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — personalized multi-course Costa Rican menu with wine pairing selected by the resort's sommelier

day_by_day.notes: This transfer day marks the return to the resort for the final two nights. If taking the charter flight, book well in advance. The scenic flight over Arenal Volcano, cloud forests, and the Pacific coastline is itself a premium experience worth the investment.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise horseback riding along the Pacific beach — a quintessential Costa Rican experience with dramatic coastal scenery. Expert guides lead you along the shoreline as the sun rises over the jungle-backed coast. Return to the resort for a late breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to a nearby offshore reef or island (Isla del Caño or equivalent premium dive site). Explore vibrant coral gardens, sea turtles, rays, and tropical fish with a certified dive master. Return to resort for a spa afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell experience: private bonfire dinner on the beach with a personal butler, live acoustic Costa Rican music, and a custom cocktail menu. Celebrate the final full evening in paradise.

meals.breakfast: Post-ride late breakfast at the resort — full tropical spread, smoothie bowls, freshly baked pastries, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside grill lunch at the resort — fresh grilled fish, ceviche, tropical salads, cold drinks
meals.dinner: Private bonfire beach dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — whole roasted fish, lobster, grilled vegetables, tropical desserts, premium cocktails and wines

day_by_day.notes: Confirm horseback riding and diving excursions with the resort concierge. February's calm Pacific seas make for excellent diving conditions. The private bonfire dinner should be arranged at least 48 hours in advance with the resort's events team — request personalized touches such as floral arrangements, custom cocktails, or a special cake if celebrating an occasion.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beach or a last yoga session on the resort's ocean terrace. Leisurely last breakfast at the resort — take time to savor the flavors and views one final time. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout if flight allows. Final dip in the ocean or pool. Visit the resort boutique for premium Costa Rican souvenirs — artisan coffee, locally made chocolate, handcrafted jewelry. Private luxury transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica — carry memories of cloud forests, volcanic landscapes, Pacific sunsets, and extraordinary wildlife encounters.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — the full premium spread, made-to-order eggs, tropical fruits, specialty Costa Rican coffee and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport lounge before departure — ceviche, sandwiches, fresh juices
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout (2:00–3:00 PM) through the resort concierge to maximize your final morning. Confirm airport transfer timing based on your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Consider purchasing premium Costa Rican coffee (Café Britt Peaberry or Dota Estate) as a take-home gift — available at the airport's duty-free shops.

query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami
